Estimate a psychometric network with any of the package's estimators

Source: R/psychnet.R
psychnet.Rd

psychnet() estimates a psychometric network with any of the cross-sectional estimators, selected by method. A psychometric network represents variables, such as questionnaire items, symptoms or behaviours, as nodes and their conditional or marginal associations as edges.

The estimators differ in what an edge means: partial-correlation networks describe the association between two variables after controlling for all others, regularized networks retain only the associations the data support, and Ising and mixed graphical models apply the same idea to binary and mixed data. Besides method, the arguments select the variables (vars), estimate one network per group (group), scale each variable within persons first (within), or treat data as an event log (actor, action, session, time), which is converted to action frequencies per occasion before a network is estimated.

psychnet() returns a fitted network; with group, one network per group, and for some event data a pair of within-actor and between-actor networks.

Each method can also be called directly, which exposes its full set of options. Panel data measured in a few waves are modelled by panel_gvar(), which psychnet() does not route. The method-specific pages describe each model: ebic_glasso(), ggm_modselect(), huge_network(), tmfg_network(), logo_network(), relimp_network(), cor_network(), pcor_network(), ising_fit(), ising_sampler() and mgm_fit().

Usage

psychnet(
  data,
  method = c("glasso", "cor", "pcor", "ising", "mgm", "huge", "ggm", "tmfg", "logo",
    "relimp", "ising_sampler"),
  threshold = 0,
  gamma = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  vars = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  within = NULL,
  source = c("auto", "data", "eventdata"),
  actor = NULL,
  action = "Action",
  session = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  compute_sessions = TRUE,
  time_threshold = 900,
  id = NULL,
  standardize = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or matrix with one row per observation and one column per variable, or a long event log (one row per event).

method

The estimator, a single name: "glasso" (default), "ggm", "huge", "tmfg", "logo", "relimp", "cor", "pcor", "ising", "ising_sampler" or "mgm", or a qgraph/bootnet alias. Event data accept "glasso", "pcor", "ggm", "huge", "tmfg" and "logo".

threshold

Absolute edge weight below which edges are set to zero, for "cor", "pcor", "glasso", "huge", "ggm" and "logo": a single number >= 0 (default 0). For "mgm", give its rule ("LW", "HW" or "none"); the default 0 leaves the mgm_fit() default in place.

gamma

EBIC hyperparameter for "glasso", "huge", "ggm", "ising" and "mgm". NULL (default) keeps each method's own default.

labels

Optional node labels, one per node.

vars

The variables to use as nodes (default: all). A name range (motivation:regulation), an index range (3:9), names (c(joy, fear) or c("joy", "fear")) or a single name, as in the select argument of subset(). For an event log the actions are the nodes.

group

Optional grouping column(s). One network is estimated per level and a psychnet_group is returned.

within

Optional person-identifier column. Each variable is centred and scaled within persons over all rows before estimation (each person's mean subtracted and the result divided by the person's standard deviation, as mlVAR::mlVAR(scaleWithin = TRUE)), and the person column is not a node. With group, rows are matched by person so that net_compare() can pair two levels (paired = TRUE). Without group, a person's rows are pooled and are not independent. Numeric tables only.

source

Kind of input: "auto" (default; an event log when actor or id is given, otherwise a numeric table), "data" or "eventdata".

actor, action, session, time

Event-log columns: the actor, the action (default "Action"), an optional session within actor, and an optional time used only to split actors into sessions. Giving actor selects event data.

compute_sessions, time_threshold

Whether to split each actor into sessions where the gap in time exceeds time_threshold (defaults TRUE and 900, i.e. 15 minutes for times in seconds). Has no effect without time.

id

Actor column of an event log already reduced to a numeric table with one row per occasion.

standardize

For event data with several occasions per actor: TRUE (default) centres each actor's occasions and fits one network; FALSE returns separate within-actor and between-actor networks.

...

Further arguments for the estimator, such as cor_method for the correlation-based methods, npn for "huge", rule for the Ising methods and alpha for "cor", "pcor" and "ising_sampler". For an event table, na_method = "listwise" removes incomplete rows before centring; "pairwise" (default) uses the available values.

Value

A fitted network of class psychnet (psychnet); with group, a psychnet_group with one network per level; for event data with several occasions per actor and standardize = FALSE, a psychnet_multilevel pair of within-actor and between-actor networks. Edges are read with as.data.frame().

Details

method accepts the package's short names and the names used by qgraph and bootnet ("EBICglasso", "ggmModSelect", "TMFG", "LoGo", "IsingFit", "IsingSampler"), ignoring case and separators; all resolve to the same estimators, and the fitted network records the short name. net_crosswalk() maps the arguments of the reference packages to those of this package.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when method has several values or is unknown, vars names a missing column, within does not name one column of a numeric table, or event data are combined with a method other than the Gaussian ones; psychnet_ignored_argument (warning) when threshold or gamma is set for a method that does not use it. With group, the conditions listed in psychnet_group. The chosen estimator raises its own conditions.

See also

psychnet for the fitted object; certificate() to check a regularized fit; net_centralities(), net_boot() and net_compare() for analyses of fitted networks; event_frequencies() for the event-log conversion.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(stats::rnorm(200 * 5), 200, 5)
colnames(x) <- c("joy", "fear", "calm", "anger", "trust")
psychnet(x, method = "glasso")
#> <psychnet> glasso network
#>   nodes: 5   edges: 0   (undirected)
#>   lambda: 0.06852   gamma: 0.5
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 1.39e-17
psychnet(x, method = "pcor", vars = joy:anger)     # name range
#> <psychnet> pcor network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 6   (undirected)
psychnet(x, method = "glasso", vars = 1:3)         # index range
#> <psychnet> glasso network
#>   nodes: 3   edges: 0   (undirected)
#>   lambda: 0.06817   gamma: 0.5
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 0.00e+00
psychnet(x, method = "EBICglasso")                 # qgraph alias, same result
#> <psychnet> glasso network
#>   nodes: 5   edges: 0   (undirected)
#>   lambda: 0.06852   gamma: 0.5
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 1.39e-17

ev <- data.frame(
  Actor  = rep(paste0("s", 1:30), each = 20),
  Action = sample(c("read", "quiz", "note", "watch"), 600, replace = TRUE))
psychnet(ev, actor = "Actor", action = "Action")   # event data, auto-detected
#> <psychnet> glasso network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 6   (undirected)
#>   lambda: 0.004501   gamma: 0.5
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 1.07e-09

d <- data.frame(g = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 100),
                matrix(stats::rnorm(200 * 4), 200, 4,
                       dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("V", 1:4))))
psychnet(d, method = "glasso", group = "g")         # one network per level
#> <psychnet_group> 2 networks by g (method: glasso)
#>  group nodes edges   n
#>      A     4     0 100
#>      B     4     0 100

# Within-person networks, one per week, scaled within each student over all
# four weeks; compare two weeks (paired by student automatically).
nets <- psychnet(srl_panel, vars = efficacy:anxiety, group = "week",
                 within = "student")
nets
#> <psychnet_group> 4 networks by week (method: glasso)
#>  group nodes edges   n
#>      1     5     6 100
#>      2     5     6 100
#>      3     5     7 100
#>      4     5     7 100
set.seed(1)
net_compare(nets, c(1, 4), iter = 3)  # iter >= 1000 in practice
#> Network Comparison Test: 1 vs 4
#> 3 permutations, paired groups, n = 100 and 100
#> 
#>   Test                  Statistic       p
#>   M  network structure      0.084   1.000 
#>   S  global strength        0.006   1.000 
#>        1 1.516 vs 4 1.510
#>   E  edges differing      0 of 10
#> 
#>   Edges, largest difference first
#>   Edge                       1       4  |diff|       p
#>   planning - effort      0.115   0.199   0.084   0.250 
#>   effort - enjoyment     0.382   0.314   0.068   0.750 
#>   efficacy - anxiety     0.000   0.064   0.064   0.250 
#>   efficacy - planning    0.503   0.440   0.063   1.000 
#>   efficacy - effort      0.312   0.358   0.046   1.000 
#>   planning - enjoyment   0.165   0.125   0.040   0.500 
#>   efficacy - enjoyment   0.039   0.011   0.029   1.000 
#>   effort - anxiety       0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   enjoyment - anxiety    0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   planning - anxiety     0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#> 
#>   * p < 0.05
